chunks: The narration of Sa'd from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn:
Like that, and he added: “There is no harm in fat and oil, when they affect the garment, that one should pray in it.”

key_terms.الزَّيْتِ: oil mentioned as a substance on clothing
key_terms.السَّمْنِ: fat or clarified butter mentioned as a substance on clothing
key_terms.سَعْدٍ: Sa'd, a narrator in the sanad
key_terms.فِيهِ: in it, meaning in that garment
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in clothes stained with fat or oil?
ai.summary: This report conveys a legal ruling regarding ritual purity and salat (prayer). It states that if fat or oil gets onto a garment, there is no problem in performing salat (prayer) while wearing it, indicating that such substances do not prevent prayer in the garment.
